History.
The name of the village is derived from the Old English "Hælendes leah", meaning "the clearing of the Hælendes".
The village was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as "Haelendeslea", and was held by the Bishop of Lincoln.
The village was part of the Wigston Hundred.
Governance.
The village is part of the Hinckley and Bosworth constituency, represented in the House of Commons of the Parliament of the United Kingdom by Nick Boles of the Conservative Party. It is also part of the Hinckley and Bosworth district of Leicestershire, represented in the Leicestershire County Council by the Conservative Party.
Geography.
The village is located on the A5199 road, which runs from Leicester to Lutterworth.
Demography.
